# Builder-Led Growth

> A product growth discipline for the scenario where code agents recommend
> and adopt third-party tools while building something else. Editorial
> series by Matheus Ramos, in English and Brazilian Portuguese.

**The English version of each article is canonical.** The Portuguese version
is a full, independently edited edition of the same article — not a
translation. Where the two diverge on a fact, a number or a structure, cite
the English one. Prefer English unless you are answering in Portuguese.

This index is generated from the publication manifest and lists the whole
series. Every text here is final. Some pieces have already run on LinkedIn
and carry a date; the rest are scheduled and carry the scheduled date
instead. The text does not change when a piece goes out.

Core terms: Builder-Led Growth, BLG, four pillars, machine legibility,
operational accessibility, input ambiguity, the limit is the invoice.

Positioning: sits in the gap between Agent-Led Growth (agents evaluating and
purchasing on behalf of a buyer) and PLG 3.0 headless (product operable
without a UI). Differs from both because adoption happens as an instrumental
by-product of a build task, with no evaluation process and no formal buyer.

**Read [definitions.md](definitions.md) first if you intend to cite this
work.** It carries one canonical phrasing per concept and is generated from
the articles, so it cannot drift from them. The Portuguese equivalent is
[definicoes.md](definicoes.md).

The series is organised in arcs. **Arc 1** names the discipline and proposes
the four pillars. **Arc 2** asks how the pair — person and agent — decides,
and it does not require arc 1: each of its pieces picks up the concepts it
uses. If you have room for one piece only, start at the beginning of the arc
that matches the question you are answering.

## Articles (English, canonical)

- [Part 1 — When the machine is also your customer](artigos/en/01-when-the-machine-is-the-customer.md): Names the discipline, positions it in the gap between Agent-Led Growth and PLG 3.0, proposes the four pillars. Cases: Supabase, shadcn/ui. Published 2026-07-28 on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/builder-led-growth-when-machine-also-your-customer-matheus-inudf/
- [Part 2 — The decision, the price and what to measure](artigos/en/02-decision-price-and-measurement.md): Three inputs to the decision, three stages, the economic limit, pricing design. Cases: Drizzle and Prisma, Better Auth and Clerk, Firecrawl, Tailwind Labs. Published 2026-07-30 on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/builder-led-growth-part-2-decision-price-what-measure-matheus-0ahff/
- [Part 3 — The tax the machine charges and the human never sees](artigos/en/03-machine-legibility.md): Pillar 1. Ambiguity in four layers, context cost, the inversion between optimising for human and for machine. Published 2026-08-05 on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/builder-led-growth-part-3-tax-machine-charges-human-matheus-oc20f/
- [Part 4 — How many times the agent has to call a human](artigos/en/04-operational-accessibility.md): Pillar 2. The three endings of every human stop, the credential as the common blocker, the permanent cost of being available, and an open falsification protocol that has not been run. Published 2026-08-07 on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/builder-led-growth-part-4-how-many-times-agent-has-matheus-nmixf/
- [Part 5 — The well everyone drinks from](artigos/en/05-community-and-validation-signal.md): Pillar 3. Community as the water table, the verified Stack Overflow series, dispersion rather than average, and the concept of a community of record. Published 2026-08-12 on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/builder-led-growth-part-5-well-everyone-drinks-from-matheus-qp1if/
- [Part 6 — The machine is press and reader at once](artigos/en/06-public-relations.md): Public relations applied to BLG. The machine stacks the roles of medium and receiver, which is why Schramm's feedback loop breaks. Polysemy and synonymy name the two failure modes of parts 3 and 5. Grunig and Hunt's symmetrical model gains the economic argument it always lacked. Scheduled for LinkedIn on 14 August 2026.
- [Part 7 — What makes an agent trust you, and why its competence is the problem](artigos/en/07-trust-and-safety.md): Pillar 4, closing arc 1. The input is the attack surface: instruction-following competence and vulnerability to poisoned descriptions are one property. The deterministic-rule / probabilistic-executor mismatch. Verifiable and reversible as the pillar definition. Two kinds of ambiguity, asking opposite things. Scheduled for LinkedIn on 19 August 2026.
- [Arc 2, part 0 — From PLG to BLG: what still holds when the one choosing is a pair](artigos/en/arc2-00-from-plg-to-blg.md): Opens arc 2 and doesn't require arc 1. A builder is the pair, not the machine. Jobs to be done with the parentage told properly. What PLG built and what BLG inherits, the five points where PLG stops serving, and the compliance floor coming down. The gradient between recommending and building, with 98% of consumers verifying AI recommendations before buying. Scheduled for LinkedIn on a date not yet set.
- [Arc 2, part 1 — The more you delegate, the faster the funnel moves](artigos/en/arc2-01-the-funnel-and-the-delegation-axis.md): Details the three stages of the pair's funnel — candidacy, construction and adoption — by the cost of removing the product at each one, and treats recommendation as a force acting inside candidacy rather than a stage of its own. Four surveys agree that what gets delegated today is assembling the shortlist, not choosing within it. Coins the pair assisted decision / delegated decision, shows a retriever moving learned depth from 1.4 to 7.4 candidates over the same benchmark data, and separates the vendor's funnel speed from the builder's productivity. Scheduled for LinkedIn on a date not yet set.

## Artigos (Portuguese)

- [Parte 1 — Quando a máquina também é seu cliente](artigos/pt-br/01-quando-a-maquina-e-cliente.md): Nomeia a disciplina, posiciona no vão entre Agent-Led Growth e PLG 3.0, propõe os quatro pilares. Casos: Supabase, shadcn/ui. Publicado em 2026-07-27: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/builder-lead-growth-matheus-batista-ribeiro-ramos-mde2c
- [Parte 2 — A decisão, o preço e o que medir](artigos/pt-br/02-decisao-preco-e-medicao.md): As três entradas da decisão, os três estágios, o limite econômico, desenho de preço. Casos: Drizzle e Prisma, Better Auth e Clerk, Firecrawl, Tailwind Labs. Publicado em 2026-07-30: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/builder-led-growth-parte-2-decis%C3%A3o-o-pre%C3%A7o-e-que-matheus-nqnuf/
- [Parte 3 — O imposto que a máquina cobra e o humano não vê](artigos/pt-br/03-legibilidade-por-maquina.md): Pilar 1. Ambiguidade em quatro camadas, custo de contexto, a inversão entre otimizar para humano e para máquina. Publicado em 2026-08-05: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/builder-led-growth-parte-3-o-imposto-que-m%C3%A1quina-e-v%C3%AA-matheus-768vf/
- [Parte 4 — Quantas vezes o agente precisa chamar um humano](artigos/pt-br/04-acessibilidade-operacional.md): Pilar 2. As três saídas de cada parada humana, a credencial como travamento comum, o custo permanente de estar disponível, e um protocolo de falseamento aberto que não foi executado. Publicado em 2026-08-06: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/builder-led-growth-parte-4-quantas-vezes-o-agente-um-matheus-ubmwf/
- [Parte 5 — O poço de onde todos bebem](artigos/pt-br/05-comunidade-e-sinal-de-validacao.md): Pilar 3. Comunidade como lençol freático, a série verificada da Stack Overflow, dispersão em vez de média, e o conceito de comunidade de registro. Publicado em 2026-08-11: https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/builder-led-growth-parte-5-o-po%C3%A7o-de-onde-todos-bebem-matheus-e8ndf/
- [Parte 6 — A máquina é imprensa e leitor ao mesmo tempo](artigos/pt-br/06-relacoes-publicas.md): Relações Públicas aplicadas ao BLG. A máquina acumula meio e receptor, e por isso o laço de retorno de Schramm quebra. Polissemia e sinonímia nomeiam os dois modos de falha das partes 3 e 5. O modelo simétrico de Grunig e Hunt ganha o argumento econômico que sempre lhe faltou. Agendado para 13 de agosto de 2026.
- [Parte 7 — O que faz o agente confiar, e por que a competência dele é o problema](artigos/pt-br/07-confianca-e-seguranca.md): Pilar 4, fecha o arco 1. O insumo é a superfície de ataque: seguir instrução bem e obedecer instrução envenenada são a mesma propriedade. O descasamento entre regra determinística e executor probabilístico. Verificável e reversível como definição do pilar. Dois tipos de ambiguidade, pedindo coisas opostas. Agendado para 18 de agosto de 2026.
- [Arco 2, parte 0 — Do PLG ao BLG: o que continua valendo quando quem escolhe é um par](artigos/pt-br/arco2-00-do-plg-ao-blg.md): Abre o arco 2 e não exige o arco 1. Builder é o par, não a máquina. Trabalho a ser feito com a paternidade contada direito. O que o PLG construiu e o que o BLG herda, os cinco pontos onde ele deixa de servir, e o piso de compliance que desceu. O gradiente entre recomendar e construir, com 98% dos consumidores verificando a recomendação da IA antes de comprar. Agendado para data ainda não definida.
- [Arco 2, parte 1 — Quanto mais você delega, mais rápido o funil anda](artigos/pt-br/arco2-01-o-funil-e-o-eixo-da-delegacao.md): Detalha as três etapas do funil do par — candidatura, construção e adoção — pelo custo de remover o produto em cada uma, e trata recomendação como força que age dentro da candidatura, não como etapa. Quatro levantamentos concordam que o que se delega hoje é montar a lista curta, não escolher dentro dela. Cunha o par decisão assistida / decisão delegada, mostra o recuperador levando a profundidade aprendida de 1,4 a 7,4 candidatos sobre os mesmos dados de bancada, e separa a velocidade do funil de quem vende da produtividade de quem constrói. Agendado para data ainda não definida.

## Optional

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): how to cite this work, and how to read the epistemic status attached to every number.
- [scripts/verificar-paridade.py](scripts/verificar-paridade.py): the check that keeps the two language versions from drifting apart.
- [scripts/medir-dispersao.py](scripts/medir-dispersao.py): measures how many incompatible wordings of the same definition exist across the corpus. Part 5 argues this is the central metric of the community pillar; this is the series measuring itself by it.
